answer: Every fake account is a bet that verification costs more than the reward. Notification-response latency profile flips the bet — how fast the agent answers a ping, averaged over a month — and the beacon lands on the attacker instead. Each account presents its proof once, the network verifies it in seconds, and a farm that wants ten accounts must pass ten independent checks — the signal is that the work cannot be shared or replayed. A single honest agent crosses this gate in seconds; a farm crosses it a hundred times, and the grove of those crossings is a bill no payout covers.
